name: study-1-navbar
scope: Study 1: navbar transfer, Next.js donors -> React (Vite / CRA) hosts. 15 fresh hosts x 2 fresh donors = 30 tasks, none seen while building the port rules. Hosts and donors found by a fixed GitHub search (pushed Oct-Nov 2026), pinned to commits.
memory: Disabled in both conditions (no RAG, no lessons). Memory is a separate later study.
primary_endpoint: Per task: share of runs that pass all automatic checks AND the frozen acceptance contract (strict_success). Compared per task (each task counts once), sign test over tasks.
cost_endpoint: AI tokens per run and per working result (all tokens spent / runs that work), wall time per run.
quality_endpoint: Blinded side-by-side review of screenshots (desktop 1280px, phone 390px) and diffs: donor navbar recognisable, host intact. Overall = checks AND review.
budget_note: Agent alone: one-shot + up to 2 repairs. FusionEdges adaptive: rules -> verify -> report -> 1 local edit -> bounded agent (8 steps). System comparison, not equal-call-budget.
uncertainty: 30 tasks, 2 repeats each (repeats are not independent). Report all cells, failures and quota retries. Donor fidelity is judged by review, not by link assertions.
